purpose: Engineering landing catalog for controllable flux motor routes. Every scheme must have model artifacts, experiments, acceptance criteria, stage gates, and deliverables before it can be treated as actionable.

schemes.name: 负 d 轴弱磁
schemes.engineering_goal: Use negative d-axis current to reduce synthetic d-axis flux and keep high-speed voltage within the inverter limit while preserving target torque where possible.
modeling_artifacts: sim/dq_model.py quasi-steady voltage and torque equations
acceptance_criteria: target torque feasible with V_margin >= 0 at required speed
id command remains above id_min(T)
weighted efficiency is not worse than baseline
failure_modes: negative id exceeds demagnetization boundary
copper loss consumes the speed-extension benefit
low Vdc high-speed point has negative voltage margin
schemes.stage_gate: Proceed to bench only after Vdc_min, Tmax, and id_min(T) scans all keep positive safety margin.

schemes.name: MTPA/FW/MTPV 连续控制
schemes.engineering_goal: Generate continuous id/iq reference trajectories across low-speed MTPA, high-speed field weakening, and voltage-limited MTPV regions.
acceptance_criteria: trajectory has no infeasible unmarked points
mode transitions have bounded id/iq slope
torque discontinuity at transitions remains inside calibration limit
failure_modes: lookup table discontinuity causes torque step
voltage loop saturates during Vdc drop
LUT extrapolates into unverified current region
schemes.stage_gate: Proceed when LUT generation, infeasible-region marking, and derating policy are all reproducible from scripts.

schemes.name: SVPWM / 过调制 / 六步波电压利用率提升
schemes.engineering_goal: Increase usable fundamental voltage from the same DC bus to reduce weak-field current demand and extend high-speed operation.
modeling_artifacts: Vmax factor parameter in motor model
required_inputs: allowed current THD or torque ripple limit
experiments: k_mod sweep against target torque max speed
harmonic loss and torque ripple pre-estimate
acceptance_criteria: k_mod increase reduces required negative id at target speed
additional harmonic/ripple penalty stays below limit
strategy is only enabled inside documented speed/load region
failure_modes: higher voltage utilization increases NVH beyond limit
current distortion breaks torque tracking
benefit appears only at non-operational extreme speed
schemes.stage_gate: Proceed to controller implementation only after modulation sweep shows net weighted-efficiency gain.

schemes.name: 非线性磁链表
schemes.engineering_goal: Replace fixed Ld/Lq assumptions with lambda_d/lambda_q surfaces so control trajectories reflect saturation and cross-saturation.
modeling_artifacts: nonlinear torque equation Te = 1.5 p (lambda_d iq - lambda_q id)
required_inputs: id and iq axes with units
experiments: bilinear interpolation and out-of-bound rejection test
linear model versus LUT torque error scan
acceptance_criteria: table dimensions match declared axes
interpolator refuses out-of-bound extrapolation
control trajectory changes are traceable to LUT data
failure_modes: dq convention mismatch between FEA and controller
RMS and peak current are mixed
out-of-range lookup silently returns unsafe value
schemes.stage_gate: Proceed to FEA integration after schema, interpolation, and out-of-bound behavior are fully tested.

schemes.name: 磁路饱和协同设计
schemes.engineering_goal: Tune rotor barriers, bridges, PM placement, and saliency so current commands produce useful flux weakening and MTPV behavior.
experiments: FEA LUT backfeed into control search
acceptance_criteria: candidate improves target speed or weighted efficiency versus baseline
rotor stress margin passes max speed requirement
demagnetization margin passes high-temperature negative-id case
failure_modes: high saliency creates excessive torque ripple
weak-field gain is lost to iron loss
rotor bridge cannot meet mechanical strength
schemes.stage_gate: Proceed to detailed electromagnetic design only after FEA-derived LUT improves the control scorecard.

schemes.name: PMaSynRM / 高凸极低永磁占比
schemes.engineering_goal: Reduce PM flux and high-speed Ke pressure while recovering torque through reluctance torque and high saliency.
experiments: PM fraction versus low-speed torque scan
acceptance_criteria: low-speed peak torque remains above target
high-speed voltage margin improves versus IPMSM baseline
torque ripple remains inside NVH screening limit
failure_modes: low Ke sacrifices too much launch torque
reluctance torque requires excessive current
rotor barrier geometry fails stress screen
schemes.stage_gate: Proceed when PM reduction gives net high-speed gain without violating low-speed torque and NVH constraints.

schemes.name: 可变磁化状态 / Memory Motor
schemes.engineering_goal: Evaluate whether discrete PM flux states can reduce high-speed voltage demand without unacceptable switching, observability, or demag risk.
acceptance_criteria: low-flux state improves high-speed weighted efficiency
high-flux state still satisfies low-speed torque target
unknown state has conservative derating path
failure_modes: magnetization state cannot be observed reliably
pulse current exceeds inverter or DC-link capability
partial irreversible demag causes permanent torque ripple
schemes.stage_gate: Stay in simulation until state observability and pulse energy have credible engineering paths.

schemes.name: 混合励磁
schemes.engineering_goal: Assess whether field winding control can reduce total high-speed losses after accounting for excitation copper loss and thermal burden.
modeling_artifacts: equivalent psi_eff = psi_pm + kf * if model
experiments: if sweep versus V_margin and torque
acceptance_criteria: field excitation saves more loss than it adds
field winding temperature remains below limit
loss of excitation has safe derating behavior
failure_modes: field copper loss cancels weak-field savings
field winding overheats
over-excitation or loss-of-excitation fault creates unsafe torque
schemes.stage_gate: Proceed only if total-loss scorecard beats control-only weak-field route under weighted drive cycle.

schemes.name: 绕组重构
schemes.engineering_goal: Compare multiple winding configurations that trade low-speed torque constant for lower high-speed Ke and voltage demand.
required_inputs: switching hardware current and voltage limits
experiments: low-speed and high-speed configuration envelope comparison
acceptance_criteria: configuration switch improves weighted envelope versus single winding
switching point has bounded torque and current transient
fault default state is safe
failure_modes: high-current switching network is too costly or lossy
switching transient causes torque shock
EMI or insulation stress exceeds design limit
schemes.stage_gate: Proceed only if multi-configuration scorecard shows large benefit that justifies switching hardware.

schemes.name: 多相电机 / 相组控制
schemes.engineering_goal: Determine whether additional phase groups add clear value through fault tolerance, current distribution, harmonic control, or effective field shaping.
acceptance_criteria: fault-tolerant torque target is met
thermal or ripple benefit justifies added inverter channels
control complexity remains bounded by documented modes
failure_modes: cost and inverter complexity exceed value
parameter identification becomes unmanageable
fault modes multiply without safe coverage
schemes.stage_gate: Proceed only if product requirements explicitly value fault tolerance or phase-group control benefits.

schemes.name: 温度、退磁和安全保护
schemes.engineering_goal: Add safety constraints that prevent optimization routines from commanding thermally unsafe, demagnetizing, over-voltage, or over-current operating points.
required_inputs: demag curve or conservative id_min table
acceptance_criteria: all optimization candidates respect id_min(T)
thermal derating prevents continuous over-temperature
fault scans choose protection over torque tracking
failure_modes: efficiency optimization overrides safety limit
temperature estimate lag permits demag command
low Vdc high-speed point saturates without derating
schemes.stage_gate: No route may move toward bench or high-voltage testing without this protection layer.

schemes.name: 工况加权效率和 Pareto 选择
schemes.engineering_goal: Convert per-route simulation outputs into comparable drive-cycle weighted efficiency, risk, and complexity decisions.
acceptance_criteria: every scheme score traces back to a result file
decision table includes efficiency, risk, cost, and maturity
route recommendation is stable under reasonable weight perturbation
failure_modes: single high-speed metric dominates real-use efficiency
risk and maturity are excluded from decision
scores cannot be traced to simulation data
schemes.stage_gate: Use this scorecard before promoting any route from research to engineering candidate.
